notes: imdbId, poster, runtime, imdbRating and ratingAsOf are filled by scripts/resolve.js via OMDb. omdbTitle overrides the lookup title when it differs from the display title.

movies.title: The Room
movies.headline: One Man's Heart. One Man's Rooftop.
movies.blurb: Tommy Wiseau wrote, directed, financed and starred in a melodrama where subplots vanish mid-sentence and every line lands at the wrong angle. You'll laugh at the line readings, the random football, and the sheer conviction of it all.

movies.title: Troll 2
movies.headline: Dinner Is Served. Run.
movies.blurb: An Italian crew directing an American cast who didn't speak the same language, and it shows in every gloriously off-key reaction. Burlap goblins, green food, and a family vacation nobody should take.

movies.title: Miami Connection
movies.headline: Friends Forever. Ninjas Never.
movies.blurb: A synth-rock band of orphaned taekwondo students takes on cocaine-dealing ninjas. The fights are earnest, the songs are about loyalty, and the vibe is pure wholesome chaos.

movies.title: Plan 9 from Outer Space
movies.headline: The Ninth Plan Is the Charm.
movies.blurb: Ed Wood's grave-robbing alien epic swaps day for night mid-scene, recasts its star with a guy hiding behind a cape, and narrates it all with total solemnity. The ultimate starter pack.

movies.title: Birdemic: Shock and Terror
movies.headline: The Birds Have Clip-Art Wings.
movies.blurb: Hovering GIF birds dive-bomb a small town while the heroes swat back with coat hangers. Long scenes of driving, an earnest climate message, and effects that look like a screensaver.

movies.title: Samurai Cop
movies.headline: He Plays by His Own Haircut.
movies.blurb: Shot with reshoots so far apart the star needed a wig that never matches. Stilted flirting, sword fights in sweatpants, and line reads so flat they become their own genre.

movies.title: Manos: The Hands of Fate
movies.headline: The Master Would Not Approve.
movies.blurb: A fertilizer salesman's bet that he could make a horror movie. Every voice is dubbed by a handful of people, the caretaker shuffles on bizarre knees, and the pacing is a fever dream.

movies.title: Showgirls
movies.headline: She Came to Vegas to Dance Angry.
movies.blurb: A big-budget studio drama played at maximum volume. The dancing is violent, the dialogue is unhinged, and every emotion arrives at full scream. Best watched with commentary from the couch.

movies.title: Battlefield Earth
movies.headline: Man-Animals, Prepare Yourselves.
movies.blurb: Every shot is tilted, every transition is a star wipe, and John Travolta hams it up in platform boots. Ambitious, expensive, and genuinely baffling from first frame to last.

movies.title: Mac and Me
movies.headline: Lost in Space. Found in a Drive-Thru.
movies.blurb: An E.T. knockoff funded with fast-food money, featuring a full-on dance number inside a burger joint. The alien family stares unblinking into your soul the entire time.

movies.title: Robot Monster
movies.headline: Earth's Last Hope Wears a Fishbowl.
movies.blurb: The alien invader is a man in a gorilla suit with a diving helmet, operating a bubble machine in a canyon. Shot in 3-D on a shoestring, with stock dinosaurs dropped in for no reason.

movies.title: Sharknado
movies.headline: Forecast: 100% Chance of Teeth.
movies.blurb: Sharks ride a tornado into Los Angeles and the cast reacts with heroic seriousness. Cheap CGI, chainsaws, and logic that dissolves faster than the stock footage.

movies.title: The Wicker Man
movies.headline: Not the Bees. Anything But the Bees.
movies.blurb: A remake of a horror classic that becomes a showcase for Nicolas Cage running, yelling, and dressing like a bear. Every scene escalates his frustration into comedy gold.

movies.title: Cats
movies.headline: Nine Lives. Zero Explanations.
movies.blurb: A blockbuster musical rendered in digital fur technology that never quite settles on how big anyone is. A-list stars commit completely while the visual effects fight back.

movies.title: Turkish Star Wars
movies.headline: He Saved the World. With Someone Else's Footage.
movies.blurb: A Turkish space epic that splices in borrowed blockbuster effects shots and soundtrack cues. The hero trains by kicking boulders and fights monsters in foam suits.

movies.title: Hard Ticket to Hawaii
movies.headline: Paradise Has a Bazooka Problem.
movies.blurb: Andy Sidaris's Hawaiian spy romp features agents in swimsuits, a mutant snake, and one of the most gloriously over-the-top deaths ever involving a skateboard. Pure 80s sunshine nonsense.

movies.title: Night of the Lepus
movies.headline: The Hop Heard Round the World.
movies.blurb: Real rabbits on miniature sets, filmed in slow motion, presented as a terrifying menace. The cast, including a Star Trek doctor, sells it with straight-faced dread.

movies.title: Batman & Robin
movies.headline: Chill Out. Literally.
movies.blurb: A superhero toy commercial with an endless stream of ice puns. The sets glow neon, the gadgets are absurd, and Arnold delivers every line like it's a pun contest he's winning.

movies.title: Super Mario Bros.
movies.headline: Welcome to the Fungus Dimension.
movies.blurb: A colorful game becomes a grimy dystopian dinosaur city with tiny-headed goons and Dennis Hopper in a hair sculpture. Gonzo, strange, and weirdly committed.

movies.title: Street Fighter
movies.headline: Every Day Is a Holy Day.
movies.blurb: Van Damme leads a multinational strike force through a plot that ignores the game, while Raul Julia gives a gloriously theatrical villain turn. Bright costumes, bigger speeches.

movies.title: Mommie Dearest
movies.headline: Hollywood's Most Intense Housekeeping.
movies.blurb: A biopic played as grand opera, with Faye Dunaway going all in on every scene. Intended as tragedy, it became a camp touchstone thanks to its iconic over-the-top outbursts.

movies.title: Xanadu
movies.headline: A Muse on Roller Skates.
movies.blurb: A Greek muse inspires a guy to open a roller disco, with Gene Kelly tap-dancing along. Great songs stapled to a story that floats away like a laser light show.

movies.title: Road House
movies.headline: Be Nice. Until It's Time Not to Be.
movies.blurb: Patrick Swayze plays a zen bouncer with a philosophy degree cleaning up the world's rowdiest bar. Grave sincerity meets nightly brawls and a villain with a monster truck.

movies.title: Jaws: The Revenge
movies.headline: This Time, the Shark Holds a Grudge.
movies.blurb: A shark seemingly follows one family across the ocean to settle a score. It roars, it surfaces on cue, and Michael Caine looks happy to be on vacation.

movies.title: Death Wish 3
movies.headline: The Neighborhood Watch Got Upgraded.
movies.blurb: Charles Bronson turns a city block into a war zone against gangs that look like a music video. The body count is ludicrous, the villains are cartoonish, and the escalation never stops.

movies.title: Ninja Terminator
movies.headline: Two Movies. One Phone Call.
movies.blurb: Two unrelated films stitched together with new ninja footage, linked mostly by phone calls on a cartoon-cat phone. The editing creates a story that barely exists.

movies.title: Gymkata
movies.headline: Stick the Landing. Save the Free World.
movies.blurb: An Olympic gymnast becomes a spy who conveniently finds gymnastics equipment in a hostile village. The kicks, flips and parallel-bar fights are utterly sincere.

movies.title: Lady Terminator
movies.headline: She Came From the Sea. With a Machine Gun.
movies.blurb: An Indonesian riff on a sci-fi classic fused with a local sea-queen legend. Wild shootouts, wilder dubbing, and a body count that keeps climbing.

movies.title: Dangerous Men
movies.headline: Twenty Years in the Making. You Can Tell.
movies.blurb: A one-man vanity project shot over decades, so the plot keeps abandoning characters for new ones. Synth music, baffling fights, and a total disregard for story structure.

movies.title: Deadly Prey
movies.headline: They Hunted the Wrong Guy in Shorts.
movies.blurb: A man in cut-off shorts takes on an army of mercenaries in suburban woodland. Gloriously unhinged action from a micro-budget, with the stakes delivered at full volume.

movies.title: Megaforce
movies.headline: Deeds Not Words. Mostly Thumbs.
movies.blurb: An elite army in skintight gold jumpsuits rides gadget-laden dune buggies. The headband-wearing hero gives thumbs up constantly and the famous flying bike effect is a sight.

movies.title: Never Too Young to Die
movies.headline: Junior Spy. Senior Nonsense.
movies.blurb: John Stamos plays a gymnast who becomes a spy, facing a theatrical villain played by Gene Simmons. It's a Bond knockoff with music-video energy and makeup to match.

movies.title: Raw Force
movies.headline: Booze Cruise to Monk Island.
movies.blurb: A kung fu club on a cruise collides with smugglers and an island of strange monks. It throws in martial arts, zombies and pirate action with no regard for tone.

movies.title: Strike Commando
movies.headline: One Man. One Scream. Many Explosions.
movies.blurb: An Italian Rambo-style jungle film starring Reb Brown, who delivers emotion at maximum lung capacity. Explosions, heartfelt speeches, and some legendary yelling.

movies.title: Ninja III: The Domination
movies.headline: Aerobics by Day. Ninja by Night.
movies.blurb: An aerobics instructor gets possessed by a ninja spirit, mixing horror, martial arts and leg warmers. The 80s style is unbeatable and the logic is gleefully absent.

movies.title: Over the Top
movies.headline: The Whole Family Arm-Wrestles.
movies.blurb: Stallone plays a trucker who arm-wrestles his way back into his son's heart. A big-hearted family drama built around grimacing, flipped hats and forearm close-ups.

movies.title: No Holds Barred
movies.headline: The Ring Was Never Big Enough.
movies.blurb: Hulk Hogan's movie debut pits him against a ruthless TV executive and a hulking rival. The villains are cartoonish, the fights are wrestling-show big, and nothing is subtle.

movies.title: Mitchell
movies.headline: The Cop Who Couldn't Care Less.
movies.blurb: A sluggish detective who seems mostly interested in beer and naps stumbles through a crime story. The pacing alone is a comedy, and its shrugging hero is unforgettable.

movies.title: Dolemite
movies.headline: Rhymes, Kicks and a Boom Mic Cameo.
movies.blurb: Rudy Ray Moore's passion project features rhyming toasts, homegrown kung fu, and mics drifting into shots. Its homemade energy is infectious and the confidence is unmatched.

movies.title: Cool as Ice
movies.headline: Drop That Zero. Get With the Hero.
movies.blurb: Vanilla Ice plays a motorcycle rebel romancing a small-town girl. The outfits are loud, the dialogue is pure posturing, and every attempt at cool is a delight.

movies.title: Catwoman
movies.headline: Beauty Is Only Skin Deep. Literally.
movies.blurb: A superhero movie where the villain's scheme involves face cream and the hero plays cat-like one-on-one basketball. The rubbery CGI leaps steal the show.

movies.title: Space Mutiny
movies.headline: The Ship Has Railings. Many Railings.
movies.blurb: A space epic filmed in an industrial building, with borrowed space-battle effects and extras who fall over railings with alarming frequency. Reb Brown leads the charge.

movies.title: Pod People
movies.headline: Make Friends. Avoid Pods.
movies.blurb: A Spanish sci-fi oddity with a friendly furry alien, a rock band of campers, and a plot that wanders between both. An MST3K favorite with honest charm.

movies.title: Santa Claus Conquers the Martians
movies.headline: Christmas Is Cancelled. Mars Has Questions.
movies.blurb: Martians kidnap Santa to cheer up their kids. Cardboard sets, a robot that looks hand-built from boxes, and green-faced aliens in antenna helmets. Perfect December pick.

movies.title: Laserblast
movies.headline: Bad Day? Here's an Arm Cannon.
movies.blurb: A disaffected teen finds an alien arm laser and blows up cars around town. Stop-motion aliens provide the best scenes and the hero's journey is mostly pouting.

movies.title: Starcrash
movies.headline: The Galaxy Glitters. The Plot Doesn't.
movies.blurb: An Italian space opera rushed out in the wake of a famous saga. Starfields made of colored lights, a cowboy robot, and a young David Hasselhoff with a laser sword.

movies.title: Zardoz
movies.headline: The Stone Head Has Spoken.
movies.blurb: A deeply serious art-house sci-fi film where Sean Connery wears a red bandolier diaper and a giant stone head floats over the land. Ambitious, philosophical, bewildering.

movies.title: Yor, the Hunter from the Future
movies.headline: He's the Man. He's Yor.
movies.blurb: A blond barbarian battles rubber dinosaurs in a caveman world that suddenly goes sci-fi. The theme song is an earworm and Reb Brown is pure enthusiasm.

movies.title: R.O.T.O.R.
movies.headline: Justice Is Programmed. Slowly.
movies.blurb: A robot officer goes rogue in a film that moves at a walking pace even during chases. Mustaches, Texas locations, and droning narration make it endlessly quotable.

movies.title: Highlander II: The Quickening
movies.headline: There Can Be Only One More.
movies.blurb: A sequel that rewrites its own mythology to involve aliens and a planetary shield. Sean Connery returns in flamboyant fashion and the story twists into knots.

movies.title: Shocking Dark
movies.headline: Two Blockbusters Enter. One Bargain Leaves.
movies.blurb: An Italian film that borrows liberally from two big sci-fi hits and relocates the action to Venice tunnels. The dialogue is cribbed, the monsters are rubber, and the cheek is admirable.

movies.title: Abraxas, Guardian of the Universe
movies.headline: Intergalactic Police. Canadian Weather.
movies.blurb: Jesse Ventura plays an interstellar lawman pursuing a renegade across a snowy small town. Deadpan delivery, strange powers, and a Jim Belushi cameo out of nowhere.

movies.title: The Pumaman
movies.headline: Wears a Cape. Flies Sideways.
movies.blurb: An Italian superhero whose flying scenes are some of the shakiest bluescreen ever filmed. His powers are vague, his costume is a blanket, and Donald Pleasence keeps it all deadly serious.

movies.title: Lifeforce
movies.headline: They Came From Halley's Comet.
movies.blurb: A huge-budget space-vampire epic that escalates into total pandemonium in London. Intensely serious performances meet wild effects and a story that keeps getting crazier.

movies.title: Monster a Go-Go
movies.headline: The Monster Is Coming. Eventually.
movies.blurb: A film abandoned and then finished by another director years later, with narration filling the gaps. Long scenes of talking, a giant returning astronaut, and pacing that tests stamina.

movies.title: Hobgoblins
movies.headline: They Grant Your Wish. Badly.
movies.blurb: Tiny puppet creatures make dreams come true with chaotic results. Features a rake fight, a phone-sex subplot, and hand puppets with no articulation whatsoever.

movies.title: The Giant Claw
movies.headline: It Came From Space. It Has a Face.
movies.blurb: The actors reportedly didn't see the bird until the premiere, and you'll understand why. A wild-eyed marionette menaces the world while scientists deliver serious talk about antimatter.

movies.title: The Creeping Terror
movies.headline: The Slowest Terror Ever Caught on Film.
movies.blurb: A monster made of carpet slowly eats victims who must practically climb in. Much of the dialogue is narrated over the action, turning a monster movie into an audiobook.

movies.title: Eegah
movies.headline: A Love Story. With a Caveman.
movies.blurb: A giant caveman falls for a teenage girl in the desert while her boyfriend sings pop songs. Bonus: a dad who's oddly calm about it, and Richard Kiel before his Bond days.

movies.title: Zaat
movies.headline: Half Man. Half Catfish. All Grudge.
movies.blurb: A scientist transforms himself into a walking catfish to take revenge on Florida. Long underwater sequences, a philosophizing inner monologue, and a costume to remember.

movies.title: Anaconda
movies.headline: Swallowed Whole by Sincerity.
movies.blurb: A documentary crew meets a giant snake and a mysterious hunter with an unforgettable accent. Jon Voight's snarling performance and the slithering effects make it pure fun.

movies.title: Mega Shark vs. Giant Octopus
movies.headline: Two Titans. One Ocean. Zero Physics.
movies.blurb: A shark leaps out of the sea to chomp an airplane, and the whole movie builds around that kind of gleeful excess. The science is ludicrous and the cast plays it straight.

movies.title: Sharktopus
movies.headline: Half Shark. Half Octopus. All Lunch.
movies.blurb: A military experiment goes off the rails along the Mexican coast. Eric Roberts, deliberately goofy kills, and a creature design that's half genius, half CGI blob.

movies.title: Shark Attack 3: Megalodon
movies.headline: Size Matters. Scale Doesn't.
movies.blurb: A prehistoric shark whose size changes shot to shot, thanks to recycled footage. John Barrowman stars and delivers a now-legendary improvised line you won't forget.

movies.title: Bride of the Monster
movies.headline: Bela Lugosi Versus a Rubber Octopus.
movies.blurb: Ed Wood's mad-scientist tale where Bela Lugosi wrestles a limp, motorless octopus prop. Tor Johnson lumbers around, and the cops are hilariously casual.

movies.title: Werewolf
movies.headline: Howl at the Lack of Moon.
movies.blurb: An archaeological find turns workers into werewolves with some of the hairiest makeup ever applied. The cast mispronounces things, the plot lurches, and MST3K loved it.

movies.title: The Beast of Yucca Flats
movies.headline: Flag on the Moon. How'd It Get There?
movies.blurb: Shot without sync sound, so the narrator philosophizes while characters' mouths stay suspiciously off-screen. Tor Johnson lumbers through the desert as a defector-turned-beast.

movies.title: Death Bed: The Bed That Eats
movies.headline: Sleep Tight. It's Hungry.
movies.blurb: A demonic bed eats whatever lands on it, including snacks it seems to enjoy. A dead-serious art-house tone makes the premise even funnier.

movies.title: Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2
movies.headline: Garbage Day Comes Early This Year.
movies.blurb: Roughly half the runtime recaps the first movie. The rest is powered by an intense lead whose eyebrows do most of the acting and a famous suburban rampage.

movies.title: Hard Rock Zombies
movies.headline: The Band Came Back. Literally.
movies.blurb: A heavy-metal band is murdered in a weird small town and brought back as zombies. The villains are cartoonish, the music never stops, and the plot is pure chaos.

movies.title: Rock 'n' Roll Nightmare
movies.headline: The Farmhouse Rocks. The Demons Wiggle.
movies.blurb: A metal band records in a remote farmhouse full of rubber demon puppets. Jon Mikl Thor's bare-chested confidence leads to one of the most legendary finales in bad horror.

movies.title: Spookies
movies.headline: Two Movies Enter. Monsters Leave.
movies.blurb: Two separate productions stitched together into one haunted-mansion monster mash. The plot barely holds, but the creature effects are wildly inventive and wonderfully gross.

movies.title: Blood Freak
movies.headline: Gobble Gobble. Repent.
movies.blurb: A biker becomes a turkey-headed monster in a sincere anti-drug Christian horror film. A narrator interrupts to smoke and muse about life. Indescribable.

movies.title: House of the Dead
movies.headline: Game Over. Insert Coin.
movies.blurb: Uwe Boll's zombie movie actually cuts in footage from the video game it adapts. Bullet-time spins, rave kids with heavy weaponry, and editing that defies comprehension.

movies.title: Jack Frost
movies.headline: Frosty's Evil Twin Has a Pun Problem.
movies.blurb: A serial killer reincarnated as a snowman terrorizes a small town while firing off one-liners. Snow-themed kills and practical effects that look like a craft project.

movies.title: Leprechaun 4: In Space
movies.headline: In Space, No One Can Hear You Rhyme.
movies.blurb: The franchise launches into the cosmos with space marines, a mad scientist, and rhyming one-liners. It doesn't care about logic and it's having the time of its life.

movies.title: Jason X
movies.headline: Camp Crystal Lake Goes Orbital.
movies.blurb: The hockey-masked slasher is frozen and thawed aboard a future spaceship. Over-the-top kills, android fighters, and one of the funniest virtual reality gags ever.

movies.title: The Happening
movies.headline: The Wind Is Coming. Run From It.
movies.blurb: A deadly-serious thriller where characters flee an invisible threat and Mark Wahlberg reasons with a houseplant. Every bewildered line delivery adds to the comedy.

movies.title: Zombie Nightmare
movies.headline: He Swings. He Shambles. He Seeks Revenge.
movies.blurb: A baseball-loving athlete returns from the dead with voodoo help to get revenge on teen bullies. Adam West shows up, the metal soundtrack rocks, and nothing quite connects.

movies.title: Glen or Glenda
movies.headline: Pull the String. Bela Insists.
movies.blurb: Ed Wood's personal plea for tolerance, told with stock footage stampedes and Bela Lugosi delivering ominous philosophy from a chair. Earnest, unusual, and strangely heartfelt.

movies.title: Reefer Madness
movies.headline: One Puff. Total Pandemonium.
movies.blurb: A 1930s scare film so hysterical that it became a cult comedy. Teens descend into madness with wild-eyed overacting while a stern principal lectures you directly.

movies.title: Fateful Findings
movies.headline: He Hacked the System. With Emotion.
movies.blurb: Neil Breen writes, directs and stars as a mystical hacker exposing corruption. Furniture gets thrown, laptops get destroyed, and every line is delivered with otherworldly conviction.

movies.title: Double Down
movies.headline: The World's Greatest Agent Lives in His Car.
movies.blurb: Neil Breen plays a super-agent living in the desert, surrounded by laptops and talking about his own greatness. Sincere, baffling, and completely unlike anything else.

movies.title: Valley of the Dolls
movies.headline: Showbiz Has Never Been This Shrill.
movies.blurb: A glossy Hollywood melodrama with oversized emotions, iconic catfights, and performances that swing for the rafters. Intended as serious drama, now a camp classic.

movies.title: Glitter
movies.headline: A Star Is Born. Sort Of.
movies.blurb: Mariah Carey's star vehicle is an earnest rags-to-riches music drama. The romance is flat, the clichés stack up, and the attempt at grit is hilariously polished.

movies.title: Rad
movies.headline: Helltrack Waits for No One.
movies.blurb: A paperboy dreams of winning a BMX race and must choose between that and his SATs. Includes a bike-dance at a school dance that is pure 80s sincerity.

movies.title: Staying Alive
movies.headline: Broadway's Most Ambitious Abs.
movies.blurb: The disco sequel directed by Stallone builds to a Broadway show of sweaty, smoky interpretive dance. Every frame is about muscles and the finale is spectacularly overcooked.

movies.title: Vampire's Kiss
movies.headline: The Alphabet Was Never Safe.
movies.blurb: Nicolas Cage plays a literary agent convinced he's becoming a vampire, delivering one of the most unhinged performances on film. Strange accents and screaming abound.

movies.title: The Apple
movies.headline: The Future Is a Disco. Repent.
movies.blurb: A futuristic disco musical that turns into a biblical allegory. Wild costumes, wilder songs, and a plot that gets stranger with every number.

movies.title: Can't Stop the Music
movies.headline: The Disco Origin Story Nobody Asked For.
movies.blurb: A fictionalized origin of the Village People with Steve Guttenberg as an eager songwriter. Big numbers, bigger outfits, and an earnest tone that keeps it gloriously goofy.

movies.title: From Justin to Kelly
movies.headline: Spring Break. Spontaneous Singing.
movies.blurb: A musical spun off from a singing competition, set during spring break in Florida. Characters burst into song, dance on the beach, and get chased by rules-obsessed rivals.

movies.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
movies.headline: All the Songs. None of the Sense.
movies.blurb: A wordless rock musical starring the Bee Gees and Peter Frampton, narrated by George Burns. Celebrity cameos, cartoonish villains, and covers in wild new contexts.

movies.title: Howard the Duck
movies.headline: He's a Duck. He's From Space. Deal With It.
movies.blurb: A big-budget production about a duck pulled from his planet to Cleveland. The animatronic suit is weird, the romance is weirder, and the finale veers into monster mayhem.

movies.title: Theodore Rex
movies.headline: The Partner Is a Dinosaur. The Case Is Bananas.
movies.blurb: A tough cop gets paired with a giant dinosaur detective in a future city. The costume is clunky, the tone is kid-friendly noir, and it's never boring.

movies.title: Foodfight!
movies.headline: The Supermarket Never Sleeps.
movies.blurb: A long-delayed animated film where grocery mascots battle in a supermarket after hours. Stiff animation and odd jokes make every scene feel subtly wrong.

movies.title: Kazaam
movies.headline: Three Wishes. Several Raps.
movies.blurb: Shaquille O'Neal plays a rapping genie who bonds with a kid. Musical interludes, goofy magic and a friendly charm make it a nostalgic so-bad-it's-good night.

movies.title: Breakin' 2: Electric Boogaloo
movies.headline: The Rec Center Needs You. Dance.
movies.blurb: Breakdancers fight to save a community center from developers. Every problem is solved by dance, including a famous number on the walls and ceiling.

movies.title: Hercules in New York
movies.headline: A God Walks Into Manhattan.
movies.blurb: Arnold Schwarzenegger's first film, with his lines dubbed over and Olympus filmed in a city park. The fish-out-of-water comedy includes a chariot chase through traffic.

movies.title: The Wild World of Batwoman
movies.headline: Fight Crime. Then Do the Watusi.
movies.blurb: A superheroine and her go-go dancing sidekicks battle a mad scientist. The film stops for dance numbers constantly and the plot is mostly about a hearing aid.

movies.title: Hell Comes to Frogtown
movies.headline: The Wasteland Has a Frog Problem.
movies.blurb: Wrestler Roddy Piper wanders a post-apocalyptic desert on a mission that leads straight into a town of rubber-masked frog people. Cheap, cheeky and completely committed.
